rv.q: Church Hurt is a vital and compassionate portrait of how those roots nurture and strangle at the same time.
"Church Hurt" is a rich and very funny play which keenly encapsulates the fight to build a better world, with one church as its focus.
The conversations between them all are laugh out loud funny and often a thoughtful exploration of how to exist in a world where the definition of what is an acceptable identity is extremely narrow.
"Church Hurt" has good bones, and a lovely team behind it.

Shows like Church Hurt are, in every way that counts, what true Chicago theater should look and feel like; intimate, raw, mature, and intentional in their building blocks of design, writing, and performance.
Their journeys, both separately and collectively, are thrilling to watch and hear.
Keep an eye on this company; I feel they are one to reckon with.

cn.t: Critics praise this world premiere for its nuanced exploration of religious trauma and ex-evangelical experiences, with strong performances anchoring Frauenhoffer's thoughtful examination of faith, community, and healing.
